I only know the romantic version of it — the great golden age of humanity before all the problems started, and all that. A lost era of peace and prosperity. People usually talk about this time as some kind of a lost paradise."

Effie smiled.

"I guess it was, for a while. As close to a paradise as we have ever come."

She sighed.

They spent the day just resting. Nephis was meditating, eyes closed, looking pretty pale. It reminded me of the old days on the Forgotten Shore, back when we were stuck in the Crimson Labyrinth looking for that city from Cassie’s vision. She used to meditate like that all the time to deal with the pain of her Flaw. She wasn't in pain now, but losing her Domain must have been a massive blow. Still, she’s Nephis—she doesn't know how to quit. She just keeps pushing, totally obsessed with her goal. If you asked, she’d just say it’s just pain, like it’s nothing. She’s adapted to it, and she adapts to everything else too. Our strategy had to change, though. I’ve been fighting on the ground with my shadows and Azarax’s Deathless army, while Neph was taking the heat in the sky. But with her power cut down, she can’t stay up there alone anymore. So, we decided she’s moving to the ground. She’ll be healing my shades now, which should let the Shadow Legion move faster and hit harder. If she needs to, she can still use her Blessing to blast enemies. That makes me the tip of the spear, which is fine, but I need to be more aggressive. Azarax is annoying, but his Deathless are basically a giant bone shield for my shades, which helps a lot with attrition. Neph opened her eyes and looked at the Tomb of Ariel in the distance. She asked what I thought we’d find there. I didn't have a clue. The real Great River is going to be totally different from the Nightmare version. No Twilight, no city of the Outsiders, and hopefully no Plagues, though I doubt the River People survived. I’ve seen too many Nightmare Creatures from the Tomb during the Chain of Nightmares to think anything good is left. And then there’s the Vile Thieving Bird. If that thing is still nesting in the heart of the Tomb, who knows what it’s done? It could have stolen the suns or destroyed everything. Neph smiled a bit and asked if it could get worse. I told her I wasn't stupid enough to tempt fate like that. The sun started setting, and Azarax showed up, his black skeleton armor soaking up the red light. He told us to get ready because the night was coming. We stood up, and the Deathless rose from the dunes while my shadows formed up behind us. Saint, Slayer, and Serpent were leading the charge. I split into seven avatars and pulled out my Shells. Azarax started bragging about how we were heading into the inner desert where the elite armies fought, and he asked if we’d ever faced Sacred beings. I told him I’d killed a few Cursed ones, including a couple of Tyrants. Neph mentioned she’d killed a Cursed Demon. Azarax went quiet, then warned us that if we hit a Sacred beast, it’d be unkillable. I just told him if that happened, we’d just run faster than him. I ordered the march. Another night in hell.

They spent the day resting.

Nephis meditated with her eyes closed, her face pale. Seeing her like this, Sunny was reminded of their times on the Forgotten Shore — the early days spent in the Crimson Labyrinth, searching for the city from Cassie's vision.

Nephis used to meditate often back then, as well, learning how to cope with the pain of her Flaw. She was not in pain at the moment, but being defeated and losing most of her Domain must have hurt just as much, if not more.

But he knew that she would be... if not alright, then at least the same. That was Nephis, after all — she did not know how to stop. No matter how hurt she got, she continued to push forward with the same blind determination, utterly devoted to her seemingly unreasonable goal.

If he asked, she would say that it was just pain.

She had grown used to pain even before they met, and that was why no amount of anguish could faze her.

That said, her stubbornness did not mean that she was inflexible. On the contrary, Nephis could adapt to almost anything, becoming whatever she needed to become in order to overcome the obstacles facing her. At the moment, that meant that their present strategy had to change.

Sunny fought on the ground, surrounded by his shades and protected by his Shadows. As of late, there was also Azarax and his Deathless army to support the Shadow Legion in case an especially tough enemy revealed itself. Nephis was alone in the sky, though.

Dodging the arrows and javelins of the cursed prisoners of Ariel's Hell was already difficult enough, but there were also beings capable of flight among the Deathless. It did not really make sense, since nothing supported the weight of their skeletal bodies in the air, and yet it was true.

With her power severely diminished, Nephis could not stay alone in the sky anymore. So, they decided that from tonight forward, her role was going to change.

Instead of attacking the Deathless from above to make the passage of the Shadow Legion easier, she was going to be among the shades on the ground tonight. Neph's role would be to heal the shades as they were being damaged, which would allow the Shadow Legion to move much faster and face far greater threats.

And if her help was needed, she would always be able to aim the Blessing at their enemies and join the fight.

Which meant that Sunny would be the tip of the spear today. He was glad to be, but the tactics he used would need to be shifted to a more aggressive approach.

‘Despite his irritating personality, Azarax is quite useful.'

It was not just that the ancient tyrant was powerful or that his thralls were strong. The most beneficial thing about him was that his Deathless warriors could move ahead of the Shadow Legion, serving as a robust meat shield.

Well... perhaps a bone shield, in this case. The point was that their presence on the battlefield diminished the rate of attrition among Sunny's shades and allowed the Shadow Legion to be more effective.

"What do you think we will find there?"

Neph's voice distracted Sunny from his thoughts. At some point, she had opened her eyes and looked at the distant silhouette of the Tomb of Ariel. Her voice sounded even, but there was a dark undertone to it. Sunny hesitated.

Eventually, he shrugged.

"There is no way to tell."

The real Great River was bound to be entirely different from the one they had encountered in the Nightmare. That was because there would not have been a Twilight in the true Tomb of Ariel — Daeron's people had only entered the Seed of Nightmare, after all, not the actual pyramid.

It was only the Serpent King himself and a small number of his champions who had. So, there would be no city of the Outsiders on the Great River. There would be no army to lay siege to Verge, even if it had ultimately failed. This absence would affect the cities of the River People, as well, changing everything Sunny and Nephis knew about their civilization.

However... there would be no Plagues, either. Because the members of the cohort, too, had only entered the Nightmare version of the Tomb of Ariel, not the real thing. The forces of the Defilement would not have been led on a terrifying conquest of the Great River by the six Heralds of the Estuary, and so, the cities of the River People could still be intact.

Sunny did not believe that they were, though.

He sighed.

"But I am certain that it will be bad."

His opinion was based on one simple fact... it was that he had encountered many Nightmare Creatures from the Tomb of Ariel during the Chain of Nightmares. The fact that they had been able to escape the Dream Realm in great numbers hinted at the fact that the civilization of the River People had fallen, after all, and that there was nothing but Corruption in the great pyramid anymore.

And there was something else, as well...

It was the Vile Thieving Bird.

If it had really made a nest at the heart of the Tomb of Ariel after escaping the Nightmare and returning to life once more, then there was no telling how its presence affected the Great River.

That loathsome bird was a unique existence that had been hated both by the gods and by the Void Beings, which meant that it did not really belong to either side. That made it highly unpredictable... from what Sunny knew, the Vile Thieving Bird was only interested in shiny things and anything that had to do with Weaver, so there was no telling what it would do.

There was a high chance that it had left the Tomb of Ariel already, even if Sunny believed that it hadn't. There was also a chance that it simply waited in the Estuary... alternatively, it could have already destroyed Verge and eaten the First Seeker. It could have stolen the eyes of every human in Fallen Grace or Weave.

It could have even stolen all seven suns from the skies above the Great River, just to add them to its collection of shiny things.

So, Sunny did not know.

Nephis smiled faintly.

“Worse than this?"

He chuckled.

"Listen... I might be a bit oblivious at times, but even I am not foolish enough to say something like no, things just can't get any worse aloud. Things can definitely get way worse."

He looked up.

"Do you hear that, universe? I've learned."

The sun was already setting, so Azarax emerged from the deep shadows at the base of the rock formation and put his fearsome axe on his shoulder.

Deep in the shining carapace of his glass armor, the black skeleton seemed to be absorbing the scarlet radiance of the sunset.

“Prepare yourselves, waifs. The night is coming.”

Sunny sighed and rose to his feet. Nephis followed his example, her simple white tunic fluttering in the rising wind.

All around them, the sand rippled.

The Deathless warriors subjugated by Azarax rose from beneath the dunes, forming a crescent formation in front of the three Supremes. Then, an army of shades rose from Sunny's shadows to stand behind them.

The Wolf and his pack, the Obsidian Wasps, the Great Beasts of Godgrave and the Asuras of Condemnation, the Immortals of the Eternal City... and more.

Saint and Slayer moved forward to lead them.

Serpent slithered across the dunes like an onyx river, his chilling hiss reverberating under the dark sky.

Sunny inhaled deeply, feeling his strength grow as deep shadows shrouded the world. He divided himself into seven avatars and reached into the shadows, preparing to encase each in a fearsome Shell.

Azarax was already walking forward to stand at the forefront of the joined formation of the Deathless and the shades.

“Tonight is going to be different. Tonight, we will taste the true meaning of dread... the true horror of Ariel's Hell.”

His grin seemed to grow wider and more vicious.

“That is because we are close to the inner expanse of the desert. Here, only the most elite armies of the Demon Legion and the Divine Host clashed for the right to rule hell. So, tonight, we will probably face the worst fiends who dwell in this godforsaken land... the blessed land. Supreme, Sacred... have you ever faced Sacred beings in battle, Shadow?"

Sunny shook his head.

"No."

Azarax scoffed.

"Unsurprising. You wouldn't know the dread and horror of earning a deity's wrath..."

Sunny interrupted him in a calm tone:

"I did kill a few Cursed beings, though. Including a Cursed Tyrant... no, wait. Two Cursed Tyrants? One was alive, while the other was already dead. But I still killed both."

Azarax stared at him silently for a few moments, then turned his skull to Nephis. She shrugged.

"I did fight a few Cursed Ones, but I only ever killed one. A Demon."

She paused for a moment, and then added in a calm tone:

“What about you?"

The ancient tyrant remained silent for a while. Eventually, he just looked away and stared at the desert.

"Well, anyway, you're out of luck. Because if we do encounter one of the Sacred Beasts of the high commanders tonight..."

The darkness nestling in his eyes seemed to grow deeper.

“You'll get a chance to face a Sacred being who cannot be killed. Let's see how strong you are then.”

Sunny — all seven of his incarnations — looked at Azarax at the same time.

He lingered for a moment and then sighed.

"If we do encounter something like that, it won't matter how strong we are."

He smiled.

"What will matter is how swift we can run. And we can both run faster than you, so... who is really out of luck here, huh?"

With that, he commanded the Shadow Legion to march forward.

Another night in hell had begun.

Sunny wasn't entirely sure how many loops it took before he finally realized they were stuck in one. About two months had passed since that realization hit him, and that was roughly how long it took for Cassie to figure out the truth too. Now, standing on the deck of the Chain Breaker, he looked right at the blind girl. He felt a weird mix of relief, gratitude, and sheer gladness that he wouldn't have to bear the crushing weight of trying to escape Wind Flower all by himself, especially with someone as capable as Cassie.

Yet, a nagging unease lingered in his gut. How did she find out? And why?

For Sunny, the answer was obvious: the Sin of Solace.

He stayed quiet for a second, then stepped forward with a grim tone. "You see him too, don't you? Admit it. I know you do."

Cassie tilted her head, looking genuinely puzzled. "See... who? I don't understand."

Sunny hesitated. Was she lying? If she was acting, she was terrifyingly good at it—better than he ever would've guessed. But why hide it? Maybe to spare them both the embarrassment. Gods knew he wouldn't want anyone listening to the twisted things his inner demon whispered into his brain day in and day out. If she used her Ascended Ability on him, she might perceive the wraith, though it only existed inside Sunny's own head. Or maybe she just figured it out through her crazy high affinity to fate and revelations. She always had a knack for sensing things nobody else could.

Sunny frowned. "The Sin of Solace... the sword wraith that follows me around. You can't see him?"

She stared blankly for a moment, then gave a faint smile. "How can I see him? I'm blind."

She pointed at her blue eyes, making Sunny cough awkwardly. "No, that's not what I meant... whatever, forget it!"

Did it even matter? If she couldn't see the Sin of Solace, great. If she could and was just playing dumb, fine by him. Cassie had been hiding secrets ever since she became an Awakened because her Aspect forced her to know things she sometimes wished she didn't. 

Sunny grimaced, then offered a tentative smile. "Well... anyway. You really remember? That's amazing."

He let a chunk of his Shell get torn off just to create an opening. He shifted his tentacles into a forest of arms, each with seven-fingered claws, and locked the Vulture in place. The remaining tentacles turned into scythes and sliced through the tendrils connecting the Vulture to Condemnation. They both plummeted, and Sunny used shadow chains to anchor them to the ivory fangs stuck in the giant’s torso. The Vulture was fighting hard, and a tendril got dangerously close to his real body, but Sunny poured every drop of essence he had into the Shell to keep it together. They slammed into the Leech, which had been busy feeding on Condemnation. Perfect. Now he had two of these monsters to deal with. As the Leech turned its attention to him, Sunny stopped trying to win the brawl and instead funneled all his remaining power into a massive shove. He launched all three of them—himself, the Vulture, and the Leech—straight up into the black sky. His Shell was collapsing, turning into a battered sphere, but he kept pushing. They drifted through the silver essence plume and back into the dark, eventually slamming into the colossal hand of Condemnation. The hand closed into a fist, crushing the sphere and the two ancient horrors in one final, obliterating grip.

Here in the Realm of Shadows, Sunny was at home. It was a dire and perilous home, but a home nonetheless. Not only was his body and Aspect empowered by being here, but there was also a torrent of spirit essence flowing into his soul.

That was why his ability to manifest shadows had become more powerful than it had ever been, and why he was able to summon such an enormous Shell.

The vast Shell was formless, lacking a structure. But that was also a reason why he could build it, and make it span hundreds of meters — not at all inferior to the great expanse of the appalling Darkness Creature. Better yet, there was no risk of losing himself, since he was not delving into the essence of a foreign existence.

Instead, he was simply adhering to the shapelessness that was inherent to all shadows. And as a shadow himself, Sunny was no stranger to that shapelessness.

It was just a shame that his largest Shell yet was dwarfed by most of what he had encountered in the Shadow Realm, almost making him feel like he had been robbed of an accomplishment.

'Damnation...'

Of course, Sunny had no time to feel such frivolous emotions, since mere moments after forming the Shell, he clashed with the Vulture in a harrowing display of primal fury.

The rippling mass of darkness descended like a flood of hungry tendrils, and the seething mass of shadow rose to meet it midway. Their clash was both awesome and terrifying, bathed in the silver radiance of the river of essence, but seemingly devouring the light instead of being illuminated by it.

They rolled across the vertical slope of Condemnation's torso, clinging to it with dozens of tendrils and tentacles, and at the same time tearing into each other with countless more.

Hundreds of hungry maws opened on the rippling body of the Vulture, biting into the mass of seething shadows. In response, the shadows bit into the body of the dark drifter with thousands of bestial fangs, tearing it ferociously.

Torrents of darkness rained down like blood.

Even as his Shell was being ripped apart and pierced by slithering tendrils, Sunny grinned darkly in its tumultuous depths.

'Ah, this is not good…'

There was one thing he had realized in the very first moment of his clash with the Vulture… it was that the creature of darkness was an ancient evil — and much, much more powerful than him.

The gruesome damage it dealt to the formless mass of shadows was incomparably more dire than the damage the shadows were dealing to it, and just as Sunny was savaging the eerie creature with abandon, the creature was savaging him much more.

However…

Sunny was in his natural element. Every wound he dealt to the Vulture harmed the Dark One, while the Dark One was only damaging his Shell. For as long as Sunny had essence, he could freely mend and rebuild his great and formless, horrifying body.

He just had to make sure that the tendrils of darkness did not reach his actual self, and maybe… maybe, he would be able to destroy this harrowing abomination, after all.

...Or maybe he would be swallowed by one of the tendrils — hopefully dying in the process, instead of feeling the agony of his body and soul being slowly digested in the depths of the harrowing darkness first.

'No. I'll definitely kill this fiend.'

But why stop there?

Smiling crookedly, Sunny allowed a part of his Shell to be torn apart, then used the momentary lull in the onslaught of dark tendrils created by that sacrifice to launch a vicious attack of his own. The tentacles growing out of his vast Shell shifted, turning into a forest of inky-black arms, and hundreds of hands ripped into the body of the Vulture with sharp claws, each bearing seven fingers.

Holding it in place.

The only tentacles that had not transformed then changed, as well, their ends turning into scythe-like blades. Those blades then slashed at the particular group of tendrils that attached the Vulture to the body of the shadow of Condemnation, severing them all.

Sunny pushed both the Dark One and his Shell away from the obsidian surface. The two intertwined horrors — one made of pure darkness, the other from a vast expanse of shadows — plummeted down.

As they fell, a swarm of shadow chains shot from his formless Shell, wrapping themselves around the two ivory fangs that were still stuck in the shadow of Condemnation.

The Vulture tore into the mass of shadows, one of its terrifying tendrils penetrating the formless Shell deep enough to come dangerously close to Sunny's body. At the same time, the Dark One attempted to free itself from his hold.

However, Sunny poured more essence into the Shell, rebuilding it almost as fast as it was being destroyed — albeit not quite — and steering their fall by using the ivory fangs as purchase.

A few moments later, the two of them…

Crashed into the massive body of the appalling Leech, who had forgotten itself while gorging on the flesh of the shadow of Condemnation.

The more, the merrier.

Sunny's bloodlust was more than insatiable enough to accommodate a pair of primordial horrors.

Now, for the last act…

As the Leech momentarily switched the target of its hunger and Sunny's Shell became enveloped by the appalling darkness from two sides, melting between them in an onslaught of countless teeth, he abandoned all pretense of trying to attack the Dark Ones, and instead put all the dreadful power of his Shell into pushing all three of them into the black sky of the Shadow Realm.

Sunny, the Vulture, and the Leech shot away from the body of Condemnation, flying into the dark expanse of the sky.

As they flew, the formless Shell collapsed in on itself, turning into a battered sphere. The two ancient horrors were like tattered sails of darkness billowing behind it.

Of course, they never stopped shredding it with countless maws and trying to tear it apart with appalling tendrils.

As Sunny's Shell dwindled, they passed through the silver radiance of the essence plume and were enveloped by the boundless darkness once again, flying further and further away from the shadow of Condemnation…

However, they did not fly for long.

Because just a few moments later, they crashed into the palm of its colossal hand, which closed into a fist a moment later.

Crushing the sphere of shadows, and the two vast beings of darkness, in its obliterating grip.

Effie forced herself up from the mud, her body feeling like it was being torn apart. Every movement caused the sores hidden under her clothes to burst, leaking black blood. She leaned against a wooden post, watching the Steel Horde soldiers surrounding her. They wanted her dead, but she wasn't ready to go yet. She wanted to live more than ever. She looked at the soldiers, who were hesitating, and gave them a weak, mocking smile. 'Waiting for an invite?' she croaked. Her voice was thin, but it still made them angry. She spat a mouthful of black blood into the dirt. 'Look at this. I’m carrying the plague. You might kill me, but you’ll catch this rot in the process. Is it worth it?' The soldiers in the front started to panic, trying to back away, but the ones behind them kept pushing forward. Effie grinned, feeling the pain in her gut. She decided to push it further. 'There are three hundred of you. How many are already sick? Don't look at me, look at the guy standing next to you. Is he pale? Is that blood on his armor?' The soldiers started glancing at each other with genuine fear and suspicion. This was better than a fight; she was turning them against each other. If the Steel Horde was busy suspecting their own brothers, they couldn't win a war. It was the perfect rot. Then, a javelin whistled through the air. Effie realized too late that she’d made a mistake. By scaring them, she’d given them the idea to kill her from a distance. She couldn't dodge well with her hands shackled and her tendons cut, but she tried to shift her weight. The javelin tore into her side, dark blood soaking her rags. It wasn't a killing blow, but it was close. She knew whoever threw it was likely an Awakened or a Saint, someone smart enough to realize she was a threat that needed to be silenced despite Azarax’s orders. The crowd’s fear was turning into a dangerous, collective resolve. They realized they could get rid of their fear by killing her. Effie sighed internally. If she only had her essence, she could have broken these chains, taken her Transcendent form, and crushed them all like insects. She could have avenged herself properly. But she was drained, shackled, and rotting from the inside. Dreams rarely came true, she thought, watching the soldiers close in. Only nightmares did.

Effie sighed and then pushed herself off the ground, where she had been lying in a fetal position. Her entire body was a sea of torment, and as she moved, a few of the sores hidden under the layer of mud broke, black blood seeping from them.

Leaning on the wooden post tiredly, she stretched her legs and stared at the crowd of soldiers expressionlessly.

‘They are really here to kill me, huh?’

But she wasn't ready to die yet. Despite everything, she still wanted to live... she wanted to live desperately, possibly more than even before.

Effie remained motionless for a few seconds, watching the soldiers working up the courage to lunge at her, and then smiled.

"What, are you waiting for an invitation?"

Her voice was creaky and weak, but they still heard her. Their eyes ignited with murderous fury.

But Effie only laughed.

“Bastards... you don't seem to understand the situation."

She leaned sideways and spat a mouthful of black blood into the mud.

“See that? That means that I am infected by the plague. I'll kill some of you... many of you... before the lucky ones manage to land a blow. But guess what? Even those who get lucky won't live long enough to enjoy their fortune, because they'll be infected by the plague, as well. Crowding around a carrier of a virulent disease is not the brightest idea, don't you think?"

The soldiers paled. Those who stood in the front row tried to step back, but failed, pushed forward by those behind them instead.

Looking at their struggles, Effie grinned.

“But that is not even your real problem. Do you want to know what your real problem is, fools?"

She fell silent for a few seconds, breathing laboriously, then offered in a hoarse voice:

“There must be three hundred of you in that crowd, at least. You morons. How many of the three hundred of you are already infected, do you think? How many will be infected by the time you are done dealing with me? Catching the plague from me is not even the real danger. Who you should really be afraid of... is the person standing next to you..."

That made the warriors of the Steel Horde shudder. Before, they had been looking at her with murderous malice... but now, they were suddenly looking at the soldiers around them, distrust and deep, dreadful fear written on their faces. Effie could not help but chuckle.

That was what she wanted to see... that was what she was aiming for even above the deaths caused by the plague. Mutual distrust, fear, doubt, hesitation — this was the true pestilence that could destroy the Steel Horde.

After all, if Azarax's soldiers feared their fellow warriors more than they feared the adversary, how could they ever win a war? This was the rot that had to consume the Steel Horde from within.

That was why Effie smiled even as awful pain consumed her insides.

‘That's right. Look at each other. See? That one doesn't look so good. Why is he so pale? The one behind him is suspicious, as well. Is that dirt on his clothes, or blood? And the one staring at him from afar, doesn't he seem too gaunt all of a sudden?'

Her smile widened.

She was still smiling when a javelin shot from the crowd, ripping through the air at astonishing speed.

‘Uh-oh...’

At that moment, Effie realized that she might have committed a tactical error. She had missed the fact that scaring the soldiers by saying that those who approached her could become infected... might give them the bright idea of killing from a distance.

It seems these idiots were not as idiotic as she had assumed.

Effie's hands were shackled behind her back, and she couldn't really stand up because her tendons had been cut. She dealt with the previous attacks by using her legs and teeth, but dodging a javelin was a problem — especially because the person who had thrown it was obviously an Awakened, or possibly even a Master...

Or possibly even a Saint. There were plenty of them left in the Steel Horde, and while most weren't as powerful as the Dread Generals had been, that didn't mean that they were foolish or incompetent. Azarax wanted to keep Effie alive, but these officers might have had other ideas.

If someone here wasn't blinded by the same kind of unhinged lust for power as Azarax, they would see her clearly for what she was... a threat.

They wouldn't dare to kill her openly, but a large crown of angry and scared soldiers was a great cover for a bit of murder... as well as a perfect tool for it, if the unseen assailant used their cards right.

It would be quite difficult for Effie to dodge the javelin...

She still tried, though, awkwardly pushing her aching body to the side.

The javelin failed to deal her a deadly wound, but she had not been quick enough, either — it left a jagged wound on her side, dark blood soaking the dirty rags her red garments had turned into.

‘Argh...'

More pain... honestly, she couldn't even be bothered to register this source of it, by now.

The worst part was that whoever had thrown the javelin was not done yet — and their actions might have given the rest of the soldiers an idea.

Effie had successfully infected them with doubt and fear, but while the warriors of the Steel Horde were indecisive and fearful, they realized that they could allow themselves to feel these emotions after killing their source.

She could practically see the gears turning in their heads, their wary gazes turning more and more perilous.

An angry crowd was a scary thing.

‘If only I had my essence.'

Chained and surrounded by hundreds of angry men, all of them thirsting for her blood, Effie glanced at the warriors of the Steel Horde tiredly.

If she had essence, she could have snapped her chains and ripped off her collar. She could have called upon her powers and decimated these cowards. Hell, she could have assumed her Transcendent form and squished them like bugs under her feet. Sure, her insides were being consumed by the rotting plague, and she was alone... but she still could have killed them all and avenged herself on the Steel Horde.

But, well.

Dreams didn't always come true.

More often than not, only nightmares did.

Sunny had been carrying around the heavy scroll for days now, amidst all the crazy chaos of being back. A million things needed his attention after being gone for weeks, but the vessel of Weaver's will sitting inside his soul kept distracting him. Now things were finally somewhat calm, so he decided to deal with it.

He sat in silence for a bit, then smiled over at Jet.

"Well, how was it? Your little personal trip with the Lord of Shadows. Everything you hoped for?"

Jet chuckled, narrowing her icy eyes. "Oh, it was unforgettable. Effie and Kai weren't lying." She shrugged. "Though, honestly, it felt less like learning something and more like taking an exam."

Sunny scratched his nose. "Can't relate. Never took an exam in my life. And I wouldn't dare try to teach the great Soul Reaper anything anyway."

Jet looked away, smiling. "What about you? You said those trips were to prep us for the Fourth Nightmare, but it felt like you were hunting for your own answers. Did you find them?"

Sunny paused, offering a quiet chuckle. "Perceptive as always. Yeah, I actually found the answer I've been looking for since I became a Saint. Maybe even longer. Thanks for that, by the way."

He wondered why Jet always showed up with the exact wisdom he needed. Of course, she wouldn't remember helping him because of her curse, but Sunny caught himself starting to think of her memory loss as just a temporary inconvenience. Light at the end of the tunnel for everyone, really.

Jet stood up, stretching. "Don't know what I did, but glad it helped. Us outskirt rats gotta stick together. Not many left. Since the outskirts are basically gone, there won't be new ones. We're a dying breed." She deadpanned, "Or in our case, a dead breed. Whatever." She chuckled and walked off. "Find me if you need a hand, Lord of Shadows. Raising hell with you was actually pretty fun."

Sunny watched her go. She joked about being dead, but she felt more alive than anyone he knew.

He stayed in the garden a while longer, staring at the grass. The future felt heavy, but his shoulders were strong. Why was he so anxious? Everything was on schedule, yet time felt like it was running out. He sighed and held out his hand.

An ancient silk scroll materialized. It radiated a terrifying, restrained power. Despite sitting in the heart of a star for ages, it had zero burns. The spider silk was so delicate touching it felt wrong.

Sunny took a deep breath and unfurled it. Inside, black ink formed an elegant weave of runes, featuring a realistic blue snowdrop embroidered at the corner. Sunny's heart hammered; he knew Weaver had touched this.

He focused on the runes:

[Weaver was the first one to be born. And Rime was the first one to die...] 

The text told a tale of Rime succumbing to wounds and entering the embrace of Shadow. Shadow offered her eternal peace in the dark, but Rime refused, wanting the oceans, heavens, and painful, thorny flowers of life. Shadow argued that Death is inescapable, turning peace into a prison and shadows into a chain. But Rime eventually shattered the realm of the dead and escaped into the light, becoming the first to cheat Death.

Sunny stared at the story. Rime, the Demon of Repose, escaped the Shadow Realm. Very interesting relationship with the Shadow God. But then he thought—where's my Lineage? Why just a fable?

Frowning, he ran his hand over the runes and noticed a tiny bump. Thanks to Bone Weave, his fingers caught a subtle irregularity in three words:

[...A new beginning.]

A ghostly voice echoed, and the remnant Will of Weaver surged. Sunny absorbed the Spirit Weave.

'Wow. I didn't even pass out this time.'

Right as he thought that, absolute agonizing pain slammed into him.

Sunny had felt the weight of the scroll throughout the last few days, busy and chaotic as they were. A million things demanded his attention after weeks of absence… and yet, he could not help but think about the vessel of Weaver's will that lay on the altar of the Nameless Temple's replica, deep within his soul.

Now that things had settled down a little, he could finally face it.

Sunny remained silent for a long while, then smiled and looked at Jet.

"Well, how was it? Your personal adventure with the Lord of Shadows. Was it all you had hoped for?"

Jet chuckled, her icy blue eyes narrowing a little.

"Oh, it was… unforgettable. Effie and Kai weren't lying."

She fell silent for a moment, then added with a shrug.

"Granted, it was far less educational than I had thought it would be. I do not feel like I've learned something. It feels more like… I passed an exam."

Sunny scratched the tip of his nose.

"Well, I wouldn't know. I don't think I ever took a single exam in my entire life. I wouldn't presume to have what it takes to teach the infamous Soul Reaper Jet a lesson, either."

Jet smiled, then looked away.

"What about you?"

Sunny raised an eyebrow.

"Me? What about me?"

She glanced at him and shrugged.

"You said that these excursions were to prepare us for the Fourth Nightmare, but to me, it seemed like you were searching for answers of your own. So, have you found them?"

Sunny stared at her for a few moments, then turned away with a quiet chuckle.

"Ah... perceptive as always. As it happens, yes, I somehow stumbled on the answer I had been looking for ever since becoming a Saint. Maybe even longer. Thank you for that, by the way."

Why was it that every time he was in dire need of advice, Jet was right there to share some hard-earned wisdom with him? Sunny really did not know how to thank her… but then again, she wouldn't know or remember what it was that he was thanking her for. So there was no point.

For now.

'Oh.'

Sunny remained motionless for a little while, basking in the realization that he had already started to regard her inability to remember him as a temporary affliction. One that would be cured soon, no less.

The same went for everybody else.

It was as if he finally saw light at the end of the tunnel.

Jet smiled and rose from the ground.

"I am not sure what I did, but I am glad that it helped. We outskirt rats should stick together, right? There's not a lot of us left, after all. And since the outskirts are more or less gone, there will never be more. We're a dying breed."

She looked at him with a deadpan expression, then added:

"Well, in our case, I guess we're a dead breed. But whatever."

With that, she chuckled and headed away.

"Come find me again if you ever need a hand, Lord of Shadows. Raising hell with you… ah, it felt strangely enjoyable! Like that is how things are supposed to be."

Sunny watched her go with a distant expression.

When she was gone, he looked down.

"Right."

Jet always joked about being dead. But at the moment…

She seemed like the most alive person he had ever known.

"How things are supposed to be."

Sunny remained in the garden for a while longer, looking at the grass and contemplating silently. The weight of the future was pressing down on his shoulders heavily…

But luckily, his shoulders were quite strong.

"Why do I feel so anxious?"

Everything was happening on schedule, but somehow, he felt like they were running out of time. It was an ominous sensation.

In the end, he sighed and outstretched a hand.

A few moments later, an ancient silk scroll appeared on it, emanating a subdued, but terrifying sense of unrestrained power. Despite having been hidden in the heart of a star for thousands of years, it was completely intact, with not a single burn marring its smooth surface.

The spider silk was woven so finely that touching it with his mortal hand felt like sacrilege.

Sunny remained motionless for a while, then sighed and slowly unfurled the scroll.

Inside, an elegant weave of runes was painted with black ink, and at the bottom, a beautiful blue snowdrop decorated the corner, embroidered with such skill that it seemed entirely real.

Sunny trembled, suddenly finding it difficult to breathe.

Somehow, he knew that both the runes and the flower were left on the fine silk by Weaver's own hand.

Calming his widely beating heart, he inhaled deeply and concentrated on the runes.

He did not know what to expect, but... whatever message Weaver had left, it was bound to be important.

Or nebulous and mystifying. He was going to know soon.

...The runes read:

[Weaver was the first one to be born.

And Rime was the first one to die.

Broken and shattered, she succumbed to harrowing wounds and found herself in the embrace of Shadow.

And there, in the darkness, Shadow offered her solace.

"Rest well now, child," whispered the darkness. "Your torment is over. Stay here with me, unhurt and at peace."

But Rime refused.

"Your world is too dark, it is too quiet and hollow. Out there are vast oceans, boundless heavens, and flowers that bloom in the light. I want to swim in the oceans and conquer the heavens… I want to explore all of existence and gather all flowers, to bask in the beauty and enjoy pleasant scents."

"The flowers are bristling with thorns," pleaded the darkness. "The oceans are cold, and the heavens are empty. Your life was short and brutal — and now, it has come to an end. Stay with me, child. Do not refuse my embrace."

But Rime laughed.

"The thorns are what make flowers beautiful. Cold is what makes warmth desirable. An end paves the way for a new beginning. Even if I can find peace in your arms, Shadow, I want to leave. I want to live, no matter how much it might hurt."

The voice of the darkness grew cold then, turning into a terrible hiss, "But you are mine now, child. You belong to the shadows. I am Death, and no one escapes Death… not even a foolish spirit like you."

It was then that darkness became her chain, and solace became her collar.

Peace became a prison.

Time flowed, and the world slowly changed. Only silence remained the same.

Shadow refused to let Rime go…

So, in the end, she shattered the walls of his realm and escaped into the light.

That was how the Demon of Repose, who had been the first one to die, became the first one to escape Death as well.]

Sunny stared at the runes, drawn into their meaning.

'Rime, the Demon of Repose… so she was the one who had escaped the Shadow Realm…'

As expected of a daemon. The relationship between her and Shadow God was… strangely ambiguous. It was very interesting, too.

All of it was terribly interesting.

However…

'Where the hell is my Lineage?'

Why would Weaver leave behind nothing but a strange fable on the silk scroll?

Frowning, Sunny brushed his hand across the runes.

And there, almost by accident…

He sensed a subtle irregularity.

It was so minor that anyone else would have missed it. But Sunny's fingers had been unnaturally sensitive ever since he assimilated Bone Weave, so he felt the difference in the weave of the silk under a short set of runes.

'Oh?'

Just three words.

Sunny traced them with his fingers.

[...A new beginning.]

And as he did, it was as if a nebulous voice resounded in his ears, making him shudder.

He froze, realizing what this hidden message was.

It was…

It was the will of Weaver, the Demon of Fate, woven into the ancient scroll by their hand.

Once Sunny realized it, the remnant Will of the treacherous daemon surged, reshaping the world to match it.

In the reshaped world, his own Will was different from before.

He had absorbed the Spirit Weave.

'Wow. I didn't even pass out this time.'

Just as Sunny thought that, a wave of indescribable agony washed over him like a tide...

Jet knew she wasn't safe just because she’d made it out of the Dream Realm. Asterion was thorough—she’d seen what he did to Cassie—so he’d definitely be waiting at the government stronghold where her tether was supposed to be. Good thing she’d moved it weeks ago to a secret spot. Even her own cohort didn't know where she was anchored now. It bought her time, but not much. She sat up, gritting her teeth against the pain. Her armor was basically ash, flaking off in sparks, and her skin was a mess of charred black burns against her natural pale complexion. She looked like a disaster, but she was alive. Or, well, as alive as she could be. Cassie’s voice popped into her head then. System prompt: Cassie mental link active. Cassie told her to close her eyes. Jet did it, though she was annoyed. Cassie explained she couldn't risk the Dreamspawn reading her mind to find Jet’s location. Once they were done, Cassie was going to cut the connection entirely. Jet sighed, feeling the cold air bite at her burns. She told Cassie the Night Garden was gone and that the Nightmare Creature had somehow grown strong enough to corrupt Saints. It was a massive escalation. They talked about the breadcrumbs left by Saint Dar and how the Dream Merchant, Saint Thane, had been compromised. Asterion wasn't just turning people into mindless puppets; he was using them to accelerate the plague across the Human Domain. It was terrifying. Even with six Saints on the Night Garden, it fell too fast. Cassie agreed, noting the Lake of Tears had hit a critical mass. The plague was unstoppable now. Jet sat there in the dark, her body a morbid mix of white skin and black scorch marks. She predicted Bastion and Ravenheart would fall next. Cassie confirmed she’d lost track of the Night Garden, meaning the Ivory Tower was likely the next target. Jet felt hopeless. Every plan she made felt useless. Cassie told her to just hide and wait for Nephis and Sunny to get back. Jet laughed, a dry, bitter sound. She couldn't just hide; her Flaw meant she had to kill to keep her essence up. She needed a fight. Cassie told her to get out of the NQSC immediately and sent her coordinates for an escape route. It was a place no one would look, which was almost funny. Jet asked what Cassie would do, and Cassie sounded tense but confident that she had her own exits planned. Then, it was time to cut the link. Before it happened, Jet asked where Nephis and the Lord of Shadows actually were. Cassie chuckled and said she didn't know—she’d wiped her own memory of their location so the Dreamspawn couldn't pull it out of her head. Then, the connection vanished. Jet felt the sudden, sharp loneliness of her own mind. She stood up, her blue eyes glowing in the dark. Time to leave.

Even after escaping the Dream Realm, Jet was under no illusion that she was safe now.

In fact, she was confident that since Asterion had come to capture her, he would have prepared an ambush in the government stronghold where she kept her tether, as well. He had already proven himself capable of being quite thorough during the attack on Cassie.

That was why she had secretly moved her tether to an undisclosed location weeks ago, with no one being the wiser. Not even the other members of Changing Star's cohort knew where she was tethered now, so there was little chance of the Dreamspawn tracing her current location quickly.

He would find her eventually, though, so Jet had little time to waste.

Taking a deep breath, she gritted her teeth and sat up.

Her armor had been burned to a crisp and was already collapsing into a rain of dancing sparks. Beneath it, the snow-white smoothness of her skin was interspersed with gruesome burns. A good portion of her body was scorched and blackened, creating a ghastly sight.

Jet exhaled a small cloud of smoke and smiled darkly.

At least she was alive.

Well... maybe not quite alive. But definitely in one piece.

[Close your eyes, Jet.]

[Why?]

[I cannot be sure that the Dreamspawn has no access to my mind. So, it would be best if you don't show me where you are. After this conversation is over, I will erase my mark and cut our connection.]

Dar of the Maharana clan was the first Transcendent to fall under the Dreamspawn's spell... or so they had thought. It was difficult to investigate what had happened because Mordret left no witnesses, but there were breadcrumbs to be found in the last messages of Saint Dar.

The people of Red Hill had suffered from insomnia caused by a persistent plague of nightmares. Jet, naturally, was very familiar with the Dream Merchant, who had once been one of the two government Saints alongside Wake of Ruin.

It was unclear when Asterion had enthralled Saint Thane. What was clear, however, was that the unseen damage caused to the Human Domain by the infected dreams was grave. It had accelerated the spread of the plague, making countless people across the Dream Realm far more susceptible to it. Red Hill had been targeted especially severely. Much worse, the Dream Merchant had remained a subject of the Longing Domain until the very end, proving that Asterion was capable of far more than simply making his thralls blindly loyal to his cause.

After that discovery, Nephis and her allies could not even tell how many Saints had already fallen under Asterion's hex.

But, still...

Enthralling all six Saints aboard the Night Garden — including someone as stalwart as Tyris or as exceptionally predisposed to loathing the Dreamspawn as Nightwalker — was too difficult a feat. It had all happened too fast.

Cassie seemed to agree.

[It is most likely because of what happened at the Lake of Tears. The plague seems to have reached critical mass there. Now, it's... unstoppable.]

Jet was sitting on the cold concrete with her eyes closed, as if meditating. Her body was like a morbidly beautiful painting, white and black hues accentuated by streaks of vibrant red. Her expression was somber.

She remained silent for a while, then said in an even tone:

"Since the Night Garden has fallen... Bastion and Ravenheart will follow soon."

Her voice sounded hoarse in the cold darkness.

Cassie's answer was delayed by a few seconds.

[It seems that way. In fact...]

She paused for a moment, and then added calmly:

[I lost track of the Night Garden. So, an attack on the Ivory Tower seems imminent as well.]

A dark grimace contorted Jet's face.

“So... what am I supposed to do now? Every countermeasure I can think of is bound to end up being an exercise in futility."

Cassie remained silent for a while before responding.

[Put your faith in Nephis and Sunny. Hide and survive until they return.]

Jet chuckled.

"I cannot really lie low, Cassie. If I do, my essence will run out, and I'll die. No matter where I'll go, there needs to be something for me to kill there."

Cassie had to know it, as well.

[Escape NQSC for now. It is not safe there anymore... I'll provide an escape route. Once you are not in immediate danger, you can think of a way to satiate your Flaw.]

Receiving the instructions on where to go, Jet smiled bitterly.

“How ironic. But I like it, actually... that’s the last place they will look, considering the circumstances."

She fell silent for a moment, then asked: “What about you?"

Cassie's response sounded confident, but she could sense a hint of tension in it.

[If worst comes to worst... I have a few escape routes prepared, as well. Hopefully, though, I won't have to use them.]

Jet exhaled slowly.

For a few seconds, there was nothing but silence in her mind.

"I guess you'll be cutting the connection between us now, then?"

Cassie responded after a short pause:

[Yes. There is nothing left to say.]

Jet sighed again.

"Take care of yourself, Cassie."

Just before she felt a familiar presence disappear from her mind, she suddenly asked:

“Wait... Nephis and the Lord of Shadows. Where are they, really?"

There was a moment of silence, and then Cassie chuckled.

[I don't know.]

Jet scoffed.

[I don't know, because I erased my own memories of having known where they went. So, even if the Dreamspawn captures me, he won't find out.]

She fell silent for a moment.

[Take care of yourself as well, Jet.]

With that, Cassie was gone.

Jet had never really known when their seer was sharing her senses, but now, she suddenly felt lonely in her own mind.

A moment later, her icy blue eyes gleamed in the darkness.

“Right. Let's escape NQSC, then..."

And so... Sunny was leaving Vile behind, too. To be precise, he was leaving it behind as his replacement. Before entrusting the devilish creature to Saint and Revel, he convinced it to take a particular form — Sunny's own form, that was.

Vile could copy the powers of most beings whose essence it stole, and Sunny had been one of its victims. It had already showcased the ability to contain and command shades in the Tomb of Ariel, and beyond that... if it wanted to, it could create Dream Gates as well. Especially now that one of Sunny's shadows had become its own.

With its transformation into a fully fledged Shadow Creature complete, Vile was not a devil child anymore — it was a mischievous... and more than a little sinister... teenage Devil. So while Sunny indeed felt a bit hesitant to set that Devil free, he was not too worried.

That was because Saint would stay behind to keep an eye on Vile and make sure that it did not do anything too dreadful. Additionally...

Vile would spend almost all of its time on the Forgotten Shore. Sunny would have hesitated setting it loose in a place like Bastion or Ravenheart, but here? There were deadly frozen wastelands to the west, the even deadlier Nightmare Desert to the east, the Hollow Mountains and the Underworld to the south, and the haunted tangle of the Burned Forest to the north.

What was the worst Vile could do?

‘No, no... let's not think those words aloud...'

If it had been immediately after the Tomb of Ariel, Sunny might have hesitated more. But the vile spawn had lost a lot of its savage wildness over the few years it had spent in the embrace of human civilization, learning how to be more cautious.

So, Sunny had transferred half of his remaining shades to the brat, warned him sternly to be a good boy... girl... or whatever it was, and then had Saint give it a look.

For some unexplainable reason, the little wretch all but ignored his warnings, but suddenly grew demure and obedient as soon as Saint glanced at it with her cold, indifferent ruby eyes.

It was like a kid who knew that he could get away with a lot of things when dealing with his parents, but became the picture of good upbringing when staying at his strict, cool aunt's house.

‘I'm cool too, damn it...'

No, what was Sunny thinking? He wasn't and had never been that little devil's parent! He was just its temporary master!

In any case, Sunny had managed to both ensure the safety of the Forgotten Shore and further weaken his Domain with Vile's help. There were still thousands upon thousands of shades resting in his soul, many of them immensely powerful, but at least their number was not overwhelming anymore.

So...

There was only one thing left to do.

Sunny studied Revel for a bit, then smiled.

“Well? Are you ready?"

She sighed and nodded somberly.

"As ready as I'll ever be, I guess."

Sunny stood up and offered her his hand.

"Let's shake on it, then."

Revel stared at his hand for a while, then rose and took it.

As they shared a handshake, Sunny's serpent tattoo slivered down his arm and slowly slipped under Revel's sleeve. She shivered, her dark eyes widening slightly. And just like that, the bestowal was complete.

Sunny took a deep breath.

Revel would do well... he was sure she would. Saint would serve as her strength and command the legion of shades, both those hidden in her shadow and taken by Vile. Aiko, meanwhile, would handle the administrative side of running the Shadow Clan — and gods knew how capable she was.

The Forgotten Shore would endure the tides of apocalypse.

In fact, Sunny felt that even if the rest of humanity were to fall, this dark land would remain standing.

He felt a little wistful, but also content with his decisions.

‘It's for the best.'

His smile faltered a little, becoming faint.

"Hey..."

Revel's voice sounded full of some unknown, poignant emotion.

Turning his gaze back to her, Sunny raised an eyebrow in surprise.

"Yes?"

She stared at him silently for a second, then asked in the same deadpan tone:

“Can you perhaps let go now? We've been shaking hands for like half a minute..."

Sunny looked down, blinked a few times, and unhurriedly let go of Revel's hand.

His smile widened a little.

“Sure. Oh, and congratulations. I will leave these lands in your care... Lady of Shadows."

Cassie let out a quiet, dry laugh. She looked at the mirror, her expression tired. She muttered about how the Dreamspawn’s plague metaphor had stuck with her, even if the infection hadn't. She forced a smile, looking strained. She explained that her hesitation to betray the other Mordret—the one outside—wasn't just about strategy. She needed him to fall so Sunny and Nephis could return, but she realized she couldn't hide behind them forever. If they didn't come back, this was the end. No hope left if the King of Nothing won. She laughed again, admitting that despite Mordret watching her every move, she’d managed to trick him. She’d built a trap right under his nose. He wasn't as good at runic sorcery as she was, so he’d only seen what he expected to see. She’d hidden a knife in the nuance of the runes, waiting for the right moment to strike. The Mordret in the mirror watched her, silent for a long time before saying he’d been too focused on her Aspect to see the real threat. Cassie shrugged, talking about the nature of magic—the pledge, the turn, the prestige. She was unseeing, and therefore unseen. She noted that the other Mordret had been the only one to take her seriously, but even he had grown arrogant after reaching Supremacy. He’d let his guard down because he saw a mere Saint, just like they all did. The mirror-Mordret asked why she was saying this if he was listening. Cassie admitted she’d changed her mind. She was exhausted. She didn't recognize herself anymore, all these schemes and calculations weren't her nature. She compared herself to the others—the legendary heirs and warriors—while she had just been a normal girl forced to twist herself into a monster to survive. She wondered who was really shaped by the world, her or him. She used to believe in Sunny and Nephis, but realized she had set this all in motion herself. She decided to have faith in her own choices. She wouldn't betray him because he was all she had, and she was all he had. Two monsters against something worse. She touched the cold mirror, then her own blood-stained, empty eye socket. She asked if he was envious that the other Mordret needed her. He replied he didn't feel envy, but could pretend. She told him he didn't even know the man he claimed to love. She offered to share the memories she’d gathered—everything she’d seen of his life. The mirror-Mordret was suspicious, asking if she was taunting him. She said no, she was 'Song of the Fallen.' Her fate was to share what she witnessed. She could give him the memories of the years they were apart. He hesitated, then asked why she’d do that. She said she predicted he might need them. He countered that she was lying—she thought *she* might need him to have them. She just smiled. He sighed, knowing he’d regret it either way. She told him it was better to regret doing something than not doing it. He finally agreed, asking what to do. She leaned in close to the glass and told him to look her in the eye.

Cassie laughed quietly.

“Look. The Dreamspawn might have failed to infect me with the plague, but he certainly infected me with that damn metaphor. I just can't seem to get rid of it..."

She fell silent, and then forced out a smile.

“In any case, that is the reason why I am hesitating to betray your other self. It makes sense to ensure his rapid defeat to postpone the slaughter, so that Sunny and Nephis could return and save everyone. But if I can't hide in their shadow anymore? Then this is it... this is the end. There is no tomorrow, and no hope if the King of Nothing is defeated."

She laughed again.

"To tell you the truth... despite the fact that Mordret is watching my every step and listening to my every word, I still managed to fool him and build a trap for him, right under his nose. It was not that hard, actually. He is not as good at runic sorcery as I am. So even if he saw me create the array and read every rune, what was the point? He only understood enough of its general form to sate his suspicion. He didn't see — had no capacity to see — the sharp knife I hid in the nuance, to drive it into his back at the right second and destroy him."

The other Mordret stared at her from the mirror.

After a long stretch of silence, he said in a subdued tone:

“He was expecting you to manipulate his memories. He was so focused on creating countermeasures against your Aspect that he missed the real threat."

Cassie shrugged.

“Naturally he did. That is the secret of magic, after all: attention, expectation, misdirection. The pledge, the turn, the prestige... what people see, what people cannot see. Like me. I am unseeing, and therefore remain unseen. And so, they never see me coming."

She smiled faintly.

“Your other self was the only one who saw me for what I was, you know, and treated me with due diligence. But even he grew complacent after attaining Supremacy. It is in the nature of the Supremes to be overconfident and arrogant, I think. So, when he saw me covered in blood and trembling, a mere Saint, he let his guard down. Like I knew he would."

She shrugged.

"Like they all do."

The other Mordret sighed, then said quietly:

"But you are saying these things aloud knowing that he is listening... which means that you have changed your mind, in the end."

Cassie let out a bitter laugh.

"Have I? Yes, I guess I have... just now."

She raised her head and inhaled deeply.

“l am tired. I am at the end of my wits. I don't even recognize myself anymore... and not only because my own memories are missing. All this deviousness, all these schemes, all these calculations — it is not in my nature. I think I heard your other self mention once that he simply reflected the world back on itself, and was therefore shaped by the world into becoming an exceptional monster. But he had been exceptional, to begin with. They all were. Children of legendary warriors, heirs of the gods, born under fateful omens, raised and nurtured by the crushing pressure of unimaginable adversity..."

She smiled wistfully.

"But I was just a normal girl. I had a normal childhood and normal parents. There wasn't anything exceptional about me... until I was faced with exceptional challenges, and was left with no choice but to rise to the occasion. So that was what I did — right or wrong, I made one small choice after another, each twisting my form a little more. Until I couldn't recognize it anymore. So who was really shaped by this cursed world into what they are today, between Mordret and me?"

Cassie sighed and faced the mirror once more.

"I used to believe that Sunny and Nephis would return and save the day. But if I am honest with myself... it's all because of me. I set all of this in motion. I might have forgotten where they went, but I know that they left because of a message my past self had sent into the future. She must have had a plan... she must have had a vision."

Cassie's expression hardened, turning colder and darker.

“So now, I choose to believe in myself. I choose to have faith in myself. I won't hope for their return anymore, so I will not betray your other self. Because he is all I have... just like I am all he has. A couple of monsters, forced to face a far more frightening abomination."

She remained silent for a long while, and then reached toward the mirror. Tracing its cold surface with her fingers, Cassie raised her other hand and touched the blood-stained skin around her missing eye.

"But we, at least, have each other. While you have nothing. Are you envious of me? Because he needs me, while all you ever wanted was to be needed."

The other Mordret seemed to smile.

"I don't think I am capable of feeling envy, to be honest. I can pretend to feel it, though, if you want."

Cassie sighed.

"He put you in the Great Mirror and kept you imprisoned there for so long. And still, you long to be needed by him, appreciated by him, valued by him. Because you think you love him. But how can you love him? You don't even know him."

The other Mordret remained silent.

She did, as well, and then said quietly:

“But you want to, don't you? To get to know him. To grow closer."

Finally, he laughed.

"So, what is this? The pledge, the turn, or the prestige? Am I failing to see you as well, Lady Cassia?"

She shrugged.

"The greatest ruse is the one you cannot resist, even if you see it coming. But no... I am not here to deceive, manipulate, or use you. I simply want to give you what you want, for no other reason than that I can. Now that our end might be drawing close, I wanted to do something good for once, without thinking about how it would benefit me."

The other Mordret seemed to shake his head.

"Sounds exactly like something that a person planning to deceive, manipulate, and use me would say. Still... what is it, exactly, that you want to do?"

Cassie smiled weakly.

“I already said it, didn't I? My power is to see, to know, and to remember. Or to forget. And ever since coming to the Ebony Tower, I've seen, I've gotten to know, and I remembered your other self — everything there was to learn about the years when the two of you were one being, and most of what there was to learn about the years you were apart. It was like I was there, with him. Up to the point when he attained Supremacy, at least. After that... containing his memories becomes quite hard."

The other Mordret — one who had been separated from the only remaining part of himself — hesitated, then asked in a confused tone:

"Why are you telling me this? Are you taunting me, Lady Cassia?"

She shook her head.

“No. Don't you understand? My power is to see, to know, and to remember — yes. But it is also to help the rest see, know, and remember. I am Song of the Fallen, after all. My fate is to sing about those I witnessed, not to bear the memory of them in silence. In other words, just like I took the memories of a lifetime spent alone from his mind... I can share them with you. I can help you experience all the things that he experienced, so that you come to know him."

The other Mordret remained silent for a long while. Cassie waited for his response in the darkness, faced with only the coldness of the mirror under the fingers of her left hand and the hot, feverish slickness of her skin under the fingers of her right hand. Eventually, he whispered:

"Why would you do that for me?"

She inhaled deeply.

“It's because I cannot see the future anymore, but I can still predict it. And I predict that you might need these memories, one day."

He lingered for a few seconds, then said quietly:

"No... that is not true. You're lying."

He paused for a moment.

“Instead, you think that you might need me to have these memories, one day. Isn't that right, Lady Cassia?"

She smiled.

"Is there a difference?"

He laughed bitterly.

"I guess not. Ah, it's peculiar..."

There was a long stretch of silence, but eventually, he said:

"I feel like I will regret taking you up on your offer. But at the same time, I know that I will regret it forever if I refuse it... in the end, all I will be left with is regret."

Cassie lowered her head.

“Still. It's better to regret something that you did than something that you could have done, but didn't. Believe me... I know that kind of torment well."

The part of Mordret imprisoned in the mirror sighed heavily and fell silent.

After a while, he asked:

"So, what do I do?"

Cassie leaned closer to the mirror until her face was almost pressed against it.

“It's easy."

She took a deep breath.

“Just look me in the eye..."

Nephis didn't even blink, her voice dropping to a low, dangerous whisper that only Asterion and I could hear. I was still tucked away in her shadow, watching. She told him to take his hands off her or lose them, calling him a parasite. Her tone was terrifyingly flat, devoid of any human warmth. Asterion pulled back, his expression shifting into something patronizing. He commented on how much she’d grown, acting like a proud mentor rather than a target. He asked why she thought she could hurt him when he’d survived so much worse. Nephis didn't hesitate, describing exactly how she’d burn him to ash and heal him over and over until he lost the capacity to even beg. It was brutal. Asterion just smiled, unfazed.

Nephis demanded to know what he wanted. He suggested they go inside the Ivory Tower so the crowd could watch, clearly enjoying the spectacle. She finally relented, gesturing for him to enter. As he walked toward the great pagoda, passing the skeletal remains of Dragon Sevirax, the crowd outside cheered. I slipped out of the shadows the moment we were inside, my hand hovering near my weapon. Asterion looked at me, unfazed, and introduced himself as if we were at a garden party. I was furious—I’d just been carrying a bleeding Cassie across the realm boundary, and I was in no mood for his games.

Asterion walked around the hall, admiring the Gateway ring. He started talking about Nephis’s achievements, mentioning her Supremacy and how she’d taken down two other Supremes. He even threw in a jab about her 'seducing' the third, meaning me. Nephis was visibly shaking with rage. She asked again what he wanted. He claimed he was there to help. I couldn't help but laugh at the absurdity of it. He acted confused by our hostility, claiming he’d never done anything to deserve it. Nephis snapped, bringing up her father, Broken Sword. Asterion admitted he killed him, but framed it as a tragic necessity to stop the Forgotten God. He acted like he was the one suffering, claiming it broke his heart to kill his best friend.

I called him out on it, asking why Anvil and Ki Song were so terrified of him if he was such a saint. He just shrugged, suggesting that villains naturally fear good men. He even tried to justify his mind hexes, claiming he never abused the people he enthralled, just made them live 'better' lives. He had the gall to compare his manipulation to Nephis’s leadership, claiming she’d done the same thing to conquer humanity. He actually started clapping, praising her for her 'beautiful' manipulation from a position of weakness. It was sickening. He stood there, acting like he was the victim, while Nephis looked ready to incinerate the entire building just to wipe that smile off his face.

"Remove your hands unless you want to lose them. I might not be able to kill you, parasite, but I can make you wish that you were dead."

Neph's voice was even and quiet, so no one except her and Asterion could hear it… well, and Sunny, of course, who was hiding in her shadow. It was so emotionless as to sound inhuman, but the cold threat contained within it was only more palpable as a result.

Asterion broke his embrace and took a step back. When he spoke again, his words did not resonate across the lake, leaving the people watching them with rapt attention from afar none the wiser as to what was being said.

"How time flies. You really are all grown up, sweet Nephis."

He gave her an evaluating look.

"I've endured plenty of pain, you know. What makes you think that you'll be able to hurt me more than any of the countless ghastly beings that I've met?"

She pierced him with an impassive look.

"Have you ever met a being who could reduce you to a shrieking pile of charred flesh, then heal you, then burn you to ash all over again? Until you lose even the ability to curse the day you became immortal and forget how to beg for mercy."

Asterion regarded her silently for a few moments, then looked away with a faint smile.

"Ah. Still so sweet, I see."

Ignoring his nonchalant tone, Nephis allowed her brow to crease slightly and asked in a cold tone:

"What do you want?"

He gave her an amused glance.

"Are you really not going to invite me inside? I don't mind, really. If anything, talking in front of all these people works better for me."

Nephis inhaled deeply, then turned and invited him into the Ivory Tower with a gesture. Asterion walked past her and headed for the great pagoda, looking around the island.

In the distance, the people exploded with another wave of cheers. The Dreamspawn, meanwhile, studied the bones of Dragon Sevirax, the Ivory Lord, with curiosity.

Choosing not to say anything, he passed through the dragon's maw and entered the Ivory Tower.

The Fire Keepers stationed on the island had left, taking the Chain Breaker with them, so it was just the three of them inside the great pagoda at the moment. As soon as they were hidden from the gazes of the crowd, Sunny rose silently from the shadows and regarded the Dreamspawn with murder in his eyes.

Asterion met his gaze calmly.

"The Lord of Shadows… Sunless, was it? This is our first proper meeting, I think. My name is Asterion. Ah, but you already knew that."

It took all of Sunny's composure not to move. One of his incarnations was carrying Cassie across the realm boundary at that moment, his clothes soaked with her blood — so, he was in the mood to mangle and maim, not hold polite conversations.

Still, he held himself back.

Asterion looked around the great hall of the Ivory Tower, his gaze lingering on the chains forming the Gateway ring on the floor. Eventually, he let out a wistful sigh.

"You've achieved so much, Nephis."

He gave her a look that seemed almost… proud.

"No, truly. You gave me quite a start. I did expect you to make your parents proud, but I never imagined that you would attain Supremacy and conquer the world. You brought down two Supremes…"

Asterion glanced at Sunny.

"And seduced the third. How very devious of you. Well done."

Nephis gritted her teeth.

"I will repeat myself. What do you want?"

He looked at her with a surprised expression.

"Didn't I say? I want to help."

At that point, Sunny could not help but scoff.

"Please. Don't make me laugh."

Asterion sighed and strolled around the Gateway, studying the magnificent interior of the brightly illuminated hall.

"I felt it already, but the two of you seem to harbor a deep animosity toward me. I've never done anything to deserve such hostility, so I truly cannot help but be perplexed. Why do you treat me as an enemy?"

White flames ignited in the depths of Neph's eyes.

"You dare ask? I could not help but notice how you dared to utter the name of my father with that dirty mouth of yours, as well. My father, whom you killed."

Asterion stopped and turned to face her, a somber expression settling on his handsome face.

He let out a sigh.

"Indeed, I did. However, you should know by now why Broken Sword had to be killed. Do you think that I felt joy while watching my closest friend die? On the contrary, it felt as if my own heart was being pierced. But it had to be done, and so, we did it. To prevent the Forgotten God from awakening."

Nephis looked at him with scathing hatred.

Sunny smiled darkly.

"Oh… I see. You were the good guy all along. Why were Anvil and Ki Song terrified of you, then? Why did they trap you on the Moon?"

Asterion gave him a confused glance.

Eventually, he said as if explaining something self-evident:

"Isn't it only natural for villains to fear a good man? I don't see a reason why I, the victim of their treachery, should be condemned for it. Not to mention that Nephis is only alive because I prevented them from coming after her in full force. Who knows? That might have been why they turned against me, in the end."

Nephis chuckled.

"How admirable. A good man, though? How shameless are you? Would a good man put a mind hex on countless people, turning them into obedient thralls?"

Asterion smiled wryly.

"And after turning them into obedient thralls, I commanded them to do… what, exactly? Continue with their lives as if nothing was the matter, doing their best to contribute to society? How dreadful. I must truly be a monster."

He shook his head.

"Let us be honest, Nephis. Those people might have fallen under my power, but I've never done anything to abuse that power or harm them. If anything, you two are the ones doing them harm. And besides…"

He looked at her with a faint smile.

"Haven't you done exactly the same? Haven't you lied, manipulated people, and twisted the truth to win their loyalty? From the Forgotten Shore to Godgrave, you did everything you could to enthrall and subjugate those around you — that was how you conquered humanity. Ah, but don't get me wrong. I am not judging you. If anything, I am impressed… it was beautifully done, really. And from such a weak position, no less!"

Asterion raised his hands and clapped a few times, seemingly enjoying himself.

"Can you rightfully admonish me, though?"

His pleasant voice sounded a little reproachful.
